_comment: V-BRK-021 -- non-skippability, reshaped 2026-07-30 (P9-T7c-2c) from a route COUNT to four properties: MutatingRoutes() equals the registered set less a declared non-mutating allowlist; that set is a subset of 05 §1.3's route table; the allowlist is itself bounded to the three genuinely inert paths; and every mutating route authenticates at step 1 and reaches the pipeline for 3-11. The mutants attack the reshape where it is new -- a second door (M1), a door that excuses itself into the allowlist (M2), a redeclared literal (M3, M4), a bypassed registration point (M5, M6), a skipped step (M7, M8) -- plus two vacuity controls (M9, M10), because a derivation over an empty population reports the same green as a derivation over a correct one. The control for the reshape itself is NOT a mutant: dev/mutate.py has no expected-to-escape verdict, and 'the check must accept a route the design names' is a positive property, so it is TestTheSubsetArmAcceptsEveryRouteTheDesignNamesAndNothingElse in the suite. Run with `python3 dev/mutate.py verification/mutants/V-BRK-021.json`.

mutants.why: THE property. A debug apply route registered beside the real one. The old count caught this too -- but only because it was a fourth registration; this catches it because the design does not name it, which still holds when the count is legitimately four.

The subtle version of M1, and a real hole the first draft of this sweep found: the route is added AND declared non-mutating, so MutatingRoutes() still reports one and both the equality and the subset arms hold -- the route never enters the set they measure. The first draft used /v1alpha1/apply and was caught only because TestNoDebugRoutes happens to probe that exact string, i.e. by a guess. The path here is one no probe guesses, which is what forces the arm that actually closes it: the allowlist may name only the three paths that genuinely cannot write.

The exact defect this reshape exists to remove: the reporter stops deriving and states the answer. It is correct today, which is what makes it dangerous -- it stays correct-looking while the mux grows a route. The equality arm recomputes from Registered() and fails.

One level below M3: the derivation is intact but its input is faked, so every set relation is computed over a description of the server rather than the server. Behaviour-identical today. If nothing catches this, the reshape is decoration.

	out := []string{HealthzPath, NoncePath, ActionsPath, CatchAllPath}

mutants.why: The bypass. handle() is skipped, so the path never reaches s.registered and MutatingRoutes() under-reports a live mutating door. Both the uniqueness scan (two call sites now) and the 404 probe should see it; the uniqueness scan is the one that names the cause.

The registration point stays unique and stops being a recording point, which empties s.registered while the mux serves everything. This is the failure that would make the derivation report an empty mutating surface -- green by vacuity -- so the emptiness floors in both arms are what has to catch it.
Step 1 of 03 §4.1, skipped. The call-graph arm is the only thing here that reads the handler's body, and this is the clause the reshape added that the count never had.

edits.find: // ServeHTTP applies the checks that are true of every route before dispatching.

mutants.why: Steps 3-11 skipped: the handler answers 202 for an action that was never classified, planned, executed or journaled. Behaviourally this looks like success to a caller, which is why it has to be caught structurally rather than by a response assertion.

edits.find: result, err := s.cfg.Pipeline.Submit(ctx, id, env, tr)
edits.replace: result, err := s.submitRenamed(ctx, id, env, tr)

edits.find: // ServeHTTP applies the checks that are true of every route before dispatching.

mutants.why: Vacuity control for the derivation arms. Declaring the submission route non-mutating empties MutatingRoutes(), and every set relation over an empty set holds. Without the emptiness floors, M9 is green everywhere -- which would mean the whole reshape could be satisfied by a broker with no mutating surface at all.

Vacuity control for the source scan, and behaviour-preserving: the registration is spelled through a local alias, so the server is identical and `strings.Count(src, "s.mux.HandleFunc(")` is zero. A scan that finds nothing must fail, not pass -- this is the LSN-035/038 shape, and it is why the zero case is a separate branch from the wrong-count case.
